scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE, a "virtual link", which sounds
made up to me, and something around it must be wrong. I always said you can't
hold a network together with something invisible!! Could someone look at the
virtual link so the far areas are reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough four-phase investigation found no active fault in the Kath5 topology.

**Affected component**: The OSPF virtual link (VLINK0) between r4 (router-ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (router-ID 18.1.4.1), transiting through area 0.0.0.1, is the "invisible bridge" the user described. It connects area 0.0.0.2 (r8's stub area containing the 18.1.x.x/24 loopbacks and the 80.0.0.0/8 segment) to the OSPF backbone.

**Mechanism**: When an ospfd process restarts on either r4 or r8, all OSPF adjacencies drop. The virtual link cannot re-form until: (1) physical area 0.0.0.1 adjacencies rebuild (~10–40 s), (2) the SPF runs to discover the transit-area path, and (3) the virtual-link Hello exchange completes. This introduces a 3–5 minute window during which area 0.0.0.2 is completely unreachable — matching the user's report of the network "falling off the map."

**Localization**: r4 and r8 are both virtual-link endpoints. The ospf_snapshot flags (orphaned area 0.0.0.2, VLINK0 area-override) were false positives: area 0.0.0.2 has no intra-area physical neighbors (only loopbacks/stubs), which is expected, and FRR always places virtual-link interfaces in area 0.0.0.0 regardless of the transit area.

**Root cause**: No currently active configuration fault. The outage was a transient OSPF reconvergence delay following an ospfd restart on one of the virtual-link endpoints; the virtual link has since re-established with full adjacency on both sides.

**Fix**: No corrective action is required — the network is fully converged. To reduce future impact, configure BFD on the virtual link or decrease OSPF dead intervals. A more permanent fix is to add a direct physical link from r8 into area 0.0.0.0, eliminating the virtual-link dependency entirely.

per_axis.rationale: The report confirms the r4–r8 virtual-link re-established with full adjacency but does not explicitly confirm that PC0 can reach PC12 end-to-end across the multi-area fabric.

The investigation log contains direct evidence that the r4–r8 virtual link is up, area routes are present in RIBs, and end-to-end host reachability is healthy; however the agent's attribution of a past outage to an ospfd restart is speculative and not shown in the logs. Most operational claims are grounded and the diagnostic checks are comprehensive, but the root-cause inference overreaches available evidence.
